pages.caption: There once lived a poor tailor, who had a son called Aladdin, a careless, idle boy who would do nothing but play ball all day long in the streets with little idle boys like himself.
pages.description: [A poor tailor in a humble shop]
pages.scene: A poor tailor in a humble shop

pages.caption: This so grieved the father that he died; yet, in spite of his mother's tears and prayers, Aladdin did not mend his ways.
pages.description: [A boy playing in the streets]
pages.scene: A boy playing in the streets

pages.caption: One day, when he was playing in the streets as usual, a stranger asked him his age, and if he was not the son of Mustapha the tailor.
pages.description: [A stranger approaching a boy in the street]
pages.scene: A stranger approaching a boy in the street

pages.caption: "I am, sir," replied Aladdin; "but he died a long while ago."
pages.description: [A boy speaking to a cloaked man]
pages.scene: A boy speaking to a cloaked man

pages.caption: On this the stranger, who was a famous African magician, fell on his neck and kissed him, saying, "I am your uncle, and knew you from your likeness to my brother."
pages.description: [A magician embracing the boy]
pages.scene: A magician embracing the boy

pages.caption: Go to your mother and tell her I am coming. Aladdin ran home and told his mother of his newly found uncle.
pages.description: [A boy running home]
pages.scene: A boy running home

pages.caption: "Indeed, child," she said, "your father had a brother, but I always thought he was dead."
pages.description: [A mother and son talking at home]
pages.scene: A mother and son talking at home

pages.caption: However, she prepared supper, and bade Aladdin seek his uncle, who came laden with wine and fruit.
pages.description: [A magician visiting a modest home]
pages.scene: A magician visiting a modest home

pages.caption: He presently fell down and kissed the place where Mustapha used to sit, bidding Aladdin's mother not to be surprised at not having seen him before, as he had been forty years out of the country.
pages.description: [A man weeping at an empty chair]
pages.scene: A man weeping at an empty chair

pages.caption: He then turned to Aladdin, and asked him his trade, at which the boy hung his head, while his mother burst into tears.
pages.description: [A magician speaking to a boy]
pages.scene: A magician speaking to a boy

pages.caption: On learning that Aladdin was idle and would learn no trade, he offered to take a shop for him and stock it with merchandise.
pages.description: [A magician offering to help]
pages.scene: A magician offering to help

pages.caption: Next day he bought Aladdin a fine suit of clothes and took him all over the city, showing him the sights, and brought him home at nightfall to his mother, who was overjoyed to see her son so fine.
pages.description: [A boy in fine new clothes]
pages.scene: A boy in fine new clothes

pages.caption: The next day the magician led Aladdin into some beautiful gardens a long way outside the city gates.
pages.description: [A boy and a man walking through beautiful gardens]
pages.scene: A boy and a man walking through beautiful gardens

pages.caption: They sat down by a fountain and the magician pulled a cake from his girdle, which he divided between them.
pages.description: [A boy and a man resting by a fountain]
pages.scene: A boy and a man resting by a fountain

pages.caption: They then journeyed onward till they almost reached the mountains. Aladdin was so tired that he begged to go back, but the magician beguiled him with pleasant stories, and led him on in spite of himself.
pages.description: [A boy and a man journeying toward mountains]
pages.scene: A boy and a man journeying toward mountains

pages.caption: At last they came to two mountains divided by a narrow valley. "We will go no farther," said the false uncle.
pages.description: [Two mountains divided by a narrow valley]
pages.scene: Two mountains divided by a narrow valley

pages.caption: "I will show you something wonderful; only do you gather up sticks while I kindle a fire."
pages.description: [A man kindling a fire]
pages.scene: A man kindling a fire

pages.caption: When it was lit the magician threw on it a powder he had about him, at the same time saying some magical words. The earth trembled a little and opened in front of them, disclosing a square flat stone with a brass ring in the middle to raise it by.
pages.description: [A square flat stone with a brass ring]
pages.scene: A square flat stone with a brass ring

pages.caption: Aladdin tried to run away, but the magician caught him and gave him a blow that knocked him down.
pages.description: [A boy struck down by a man]
pages.scene: A boy struck down by a man

pages.caption: "What have I done, uncle?" he said piteously; whereupon the magician said more kindly: "Fear nothing, but obey me. Beneath this stone lies a treasure which is to be yours."
pages.description: [A man commanding a cowering boy]
pages.scene: A man commanding a cowering boy

pages.caption: At the word treasure Aladdin forgot his fears, and grasped the ring as he was told, saying the names of his father and grandfather.
pages.description: [A boy grasping a brass ring]
pages.scene: A boy grasping a brass ring

pages.caption: The stone came up quite easily, and some steps appeared.
pages.description: [A stone lifted to reveal steps]
pages.scene: A stone lifted to reveal steps

pages.caption: "Go down," said the magician; "at the foot of those steps you will find an open door leading into three large halls."
pages.description: [A boy descending into a dark cave]
pages.scene: A boy descending into a dark cave

pages.caption: Tuck up your gown and go through them without touching anything, or you will die instantly.
pages.description: [A boy tiptoeing through halls]
pages.scene: A boy tiptoeing through halls

pages.caption: These halls lead into a garden of fine fruit trees. Walk on until you come to a niche in a terrace where stands a lighted lamp.
pages.description: [A garden of fine fruit trees]
pages.scene: A garden of fine fruit trees

pages.caption: Pour out the oil it contains, and bring it to me. He drew a ring from his finger and gave it to Aladdin, bidding him prosper.
pages.description: [A boy pouring oil from a lamp]
pages.scene: A boy pouring oil from a lamp

pages.caption: Aladdin found everything as the magician had said, gathered some fruit off the trees, and, having got the lamp, arrived at the mouth of the cave.
pages.description: [A boy returning with the lamp]
pages.scene: A boy returning with the lamp

pages.caption: The magician cried out in a great hurry: "Make haste and give me the lamp." This Aladdin refused to do until he was out of the cave.
pages.description: [A magician shouting at a boy at a cave entrance]
pages.scene: A magician shouting at a boy at a cave entrance

pages.caption: The magician flew into a terrible passion, and throwing some more powder on to the fire, he said something, and the stone rolled back into its place.
pages.description: [A magician in a rage throwing powder on a fire]
pages.scene: A magician in a rage throwing powder on a fire

pages.caption: For two days Aladdin remained in the dark, crying and lamenting.
pages.description: [A boy alone in complete darkness]
pages.scene: A boy alone in complete darkness

pages.caption: At last he clasped his hands in prayer, and in so doing rubbed the ring, which the magician had forgotten to take from him.
pages.description: [A boy rubbing a ring in the darkness]
pages.scene: A boy rubbing a ring in the darkness

pages.caption: Immediately an enormous and frightful genie rose out of the earth, saying: "What wouldst thou with me? I am the Slave of the Ring, and will obey thee in all things."
pages.description: [A giant genie rising from the earth]
pages.scene: A giant genie rising from the earth

pages.caption: Aladdin fearlessly replied: "Deliver me from this place!"
pages.description: [A boy commanding a genie]
pages.scene: A boy commanding a genie

pages.caption: Whereupon the earth opened, and he found himself outside. As soon as his eyes could bear the light he went home, but fainted on the threshold.
pages.description: [A boy emerging from the earth into daylight]
pages.scene: A boy emerging from the earth into daylight

pages.caption: When he came to himself he told his mother what had passed, and showed her the lamp and the fruits he had gathered in the garden, which were, in reality, precious stones.
pages.description: [A boy telling his story to his mother]
pages.scene: A boy telling his story to his mother

pages.caption: He then asked for some food. "Alas! child," she said, "I have nothing in the house, but I have spun a little cotton and will go and sell it."
pages.description: [A mother spinning cotton]
pages.scene: A mother spinning cotton

pages.caption: Aladdin bade her keep her cotton, for he would sell the lamp instead. As it was very dirty she began to rub it, that it might fetch a higher price.
pages.description: [A mother rubbing an old lamp]
pages.scene: A mother rubbing an old lamp

pages.caption: Instantly a hideous genie appeared, and asked what she would have. She fainted away, but Aladdin, snatching the lamp, said boldly: "Fetch me something to eat!"
pages.description: [A hideous genie appearing before a woman]
pages.scene: A hideous genie appearing before a woman

pages.caption: The genie returned with a silver bowl, twelve silver plates containing rich meats, two silver cups, and two bottles of wine.
pages.description: [A genie bringing a silver feast]
pages.scene: A genie bringing a silver feast

pages.caption: Aladdin's mother, when she came to herself, said: "Whence comes this splendid feast?" "Ask not, but eat," replied Aladdin.
pages.description: [A mother and son at a lavish table]
pages.scene: A mother and son at a lavish table

pages.caption: So they sat at breakfast till it was dinner-time, and Aladdin told his mother about the lamp.
pages.description: [A boy and mother eating together]
pages.scene: A boy and mother eating together

pages.caption: She begged him to sell it, and have nothing to do with devils. "No," said Aladdin, "since chance hath made us aware of its virtues, we will use it, and the ring likewise, which I shall always wear on my finger."
pages.description: [A mother pleading with her son]
pages.scene: A mother pleading with her son

pages.caption: When they had eaten all the genie had brought, Aladdin sold one of the silver plates, and so on until none were left.
pages.description: [A boy selling silver plates]
pages.scene: A boy selling silver plates

pages.caption: One day Aladdin heard an order from the Sultan proclaimed that everyone was to stay at home and close his shutters while the Princess, his daughter, went to and from the bath.
pages.description: [A boy peering through a door at a veiled princess]
pages.scene: A boy peering through a door at a veiled princess

pages.caption: The Princess lifted her veil as she went in, and looked so beautiful that Aladdin fell in love with her at first sight.
pages.description: [A beautiful princess lifting her veil]
pages.scene: A beautiful princess lifting her veil

pages.caption: He went home so changed that his mother was frightened. He told her he loved the Princess so deeply that he could not live without her, and meant to ask her in marriage of her father.
pages.description: [A boy lovesick at home]
pages.scene: A boy lovesick at home

pages.caption: His mother, on hearing this, burst out laughing, but Aladdin at last prevailed upon her to go before the Sultan and carry his request.
pages.description: [A mother laughing at her son]
pages.scene: A mother laughing at her son

pages.caption: She fetched a napkin and laid in it the magic fruits from the enchanted garden, which sparkled and shone like the most beautiful jewels.
pages.description: [A mother approaching a grand throne room]
pages.scene: A mother approaching a grand throne room

pages.caption: She took these with her to please the Sultan, and set out, trusting in the lamp. The Grand Vizier and the lords of council had just gone in as she entered the hall and placed herself in front of the Sultan.
pages.description: [A woman kneeling before the Sultan]
pages.scene: A woman kneeling before the Sultan

pages.caption: He hesitated no longer, but said: "Good woman, return and tell your son that I wait for him with open arms."
pages.description: [A Sultan inspecting glowing jewels]
pages.scene: A Sultan inspecting glowing jewels

pages.caption: The Vizier, who wanted her for his own son, begged the Sultan to withhold her for three months, in the course of which he hoped his son would contrive to make him a richer present.
pages.description: [A vizier whispering to the Sultan]
pages.scene: A vizier whispering to the Sultan

pages.caption: Aladdin waited patiently for nearly three months, but after two had elapsed his mother, going into the city to buy oil, found every one rejoicing, and asked what was going on.
pages.description: [A woman running through a cheering crowd]
pages.scene: A woman running through a cheering crowd

pages.caption: "Do you not know," was the answer, "that the son of the Grand Vizier is to marry the Sultan's daughter to-night?" Breathless, she ran and told Aladdin.
pages.description: [A woman breathless with news]
pages.scene: A woman breathless with news

pages.caption: Aladdin, who was overwhelmed at first, but presently bethought him of the lamp. He rubbed it, and the genie appeared, saying, "What is thy will?"
pages.description: [A boy rubbing a lamp in anger]
pages.scene: A boy rubbing a lamp in anger

pages.caption: Aladdin replied: "The Sultan, as thou knowest, has broken his promise to me, and the Vizier's son is to have the Princess. My command is that to-night you bring hither the bride and bridegroom."
pages.description: [A genie transporting a bed through the air]
pages.scene: A genie transporting a bed through the air

pages.caption: "Master, I obey," said the genie. Aladdin then went to his chamber, where, sure enough, at midnight the genie transported the bed containing the Vizier's son and the Princess.
pages.description: [A boy standing beside a sleeping princess]
pages.scene: A boy standing beside a sleeping princess

pages.caption: "Take this new-married man," he said, "and put him outside in the cold, and return at daybreak."
pages.description: [A shivering groom left outside in the cold]
pages.scene: A shivering groom left outside in the cold

pages.caption: Whereupon the genie took the Vizier's son out of bed, leaving Aladdin with the Princess. "Fear nothing," Aladdin said to her; "you are my wife, promised to me by your unjust father, and no harm shall come to you."
pages.description: [A boy and a frightened princess together]
pages.scene: A boy and a frightened princess together

pages.caption: At the appointed hour the genie fetched in the shivering bridegroom, laid him in his place, and transported the bed back to the palace.
pages.description: [A bridegroom shivering outside the palace]
pages.scene: A bridegroom shivering outside the palace

pages.caption: Presently the Sultan came to wish his daughter good-morning. The unhappy Vizier's son jumped up and hid himself, while the Princess would not say a word, and was very sorrowful.
pages.description: [A Sultan visiting his daughter]
pages.scene: A Sultan visiting his daughter

pages.caption: The Sultan sent her mother to her, who said: "How comes it, child, that you will not speak to your father? What has happened?"
pages.description: [A mother questioning her silent daughter]
pages.scene: A mother questioning her silent daughter

pages.caption: The Princess sighed deeply, and at last told her mother how, during the night, the bed had been carried into some strange house, and what had passed there.
pages.description: [A girl confessing to her mother]
pages.scene: A girl confessing to her mother

pages.caption: The following night exactly the same thing happened, and next morning, on the Princess's refusal to speak, the Sultan threatened to cut off her head.
pages.description: [A Sultan threatening with a raised hand]
pages.scene: A Sultan threatening with a raised hand

pages.caption: She then confessed all, bidding him to ask the Vizier's son if it were not so. The Sultan told the Vizier to ask his son, who owned the truth, adding that, dearly as he loved the Princess, he had rather die than go through another such fearful night.
pages.description: [A vizier's son admitting the truth]
pages.scene: A vizier's son admitting the truth

pages.caption: When the three months were over, Aladdin sent his mother to remind the Sultan of his promise.
pages.description: [A mother standing before the Sultan again]
pages.scene: A mother standing before the Sultan again

pages.caption: The Sultan then turned to Aladdin's mother, saying: "Good woman, a Sultan must remember his promises, and I will remember mine, but your son must first send me forty basins of gold brimful of jewels, carried by forty black slaves, led by as many white ones, splendidly dressed."
pages.description: [A Sultan setting impossible conditions]
pages.scene: A Sultan setting impossible conditions

pages.caption: The mother of Aladdin bowed low and went home, thinking all was lost. She gave Aladdin the message, adding: "He may wait long enough for your answer!"
pages.description: [A mother returning home in despair]
pages.scene: A mother returning home in despair

pages.caption: "Not so long, mother, as you think," her son replied. "I would do a great deal more than that for the Princess." He summoned the genie, and in a few moments the eighty slaves arrived, and filled up the small house and garden.
pages.description: [A boy confidently summoning a genie]
pages.scene: A boy confidently summoning a genie

pages.caption: Aladdin made them set out to the palace, two and two, followed by his mother. They were so richly dressed, with such splendid jewels in their girdles, that everyone crowded to see them and the basins of gold they carried on their heads.
pages.description: [A procession of slaves carrying gold to the palace]
pages.scene: A procession of slaves carrying gold to the palace

pages.caption: He hesitated no longer, but said: "Good woman, return and tell your son that I wait for him with open arms."
pages.description: [A Sultan embracing a handsome young man]
pages.scene: A Sultan embracing a handsome young man

pages.caption: Aladdin mounted his horse and passed through the streets, the slaves strewing gold as they went. Those who had played with him in his childhood knew him not, he had grown so handsome.
pages.description: [A boy riding through the streets throwing gold]
pages.scene: A boy riding through the streets throwing gold

pages.caption: When the Sultan saw him he came down from his throne, embraced him, and led him into a hall where a feast was spread, intending to marry him to the Princess that very day.
pages.description: [A Sultan leading a prince into a feast]
pages.scene: A Sultan leading a prince into a feast

pages.caption: But Aladdin refused, saying, "I must build a palace fit for her," and took his leave.
pages.description: [A prince refusing a feast]
pages.scene: A prince refusing a feast

pages.caption: Once home, he said to the genie: "Build me a palace of the finest marble, set with jasper, agate, and other precious stones."
pages.description: [A prince commanding a genie in a grand hall]
pages.scene: A prince commanding a genie in a grand hall

pages.caption: The palace was finished by the next day, and the genie carried him there and showed him all his orders faithfully carried out, even to the laying of a velvet carpet from Aladdin's palace to the Sultan's.
pages.description: [A magnificent palace appearing overnight]
pages.scene: A magnificent palace appearing overnight

pages.caption: Aladdin's mother then dressed herself carefully, and walked to the palace with her slaves, while he followed her on horseback.
pages.description: [A bride walking along a carpet to a palace]
pages.scene: A bride walking along a carpet to a palace

pages.caption: She was charmed at the sight of Aladdin, who ran to receive her. "Princess," he said, "blame your beauty for my boldness if I have displeased you."
pages.description: [A princess greeted by a prince]
pages.scene: A princess greeted by a prince

pages.caption: After the wedding had taken place Aladdin led her into the hall, where a feast was spread, and she supped with him, after which they danced till midnight.
pages.description: [A wedding feast in a grand hall]
pages.scene: A wedding feast in a grand hall

pages.caption: Next day Aladdin invited the Sultan to see the palace. On entering the hall with the four-and-twenty windows, with their rubies, diamonds, and emeralds, he cried: "It is a world's wonder!"
pages.description: [A Sultan inspecting jeweled windows]
pages.scene: A Sultan inspecting jeweled windows

pages.caption: There is only one thing that surprises me. Was it by accident that one window was left unfinished?" "No, sir, by design," returned Aladdin. "I wished your Majesty to have the glory of finishing this palace."
pages.description: [An unfinished window in the palace]
pages.scene: An unfinished window in the palace

pages.caption: The Sultan was pleased, and sent for the best jewelers in the city. He showed them the unfinished window, and bade them fit it up like the others.
pages.description: [Jewelers working on the window]
pages.scene: Jewelers working on the window

pages.caption: Aladdin, knowing that their task was vain, bade them undo their work and carry the jewels back, and the genie finished the window at his command.
pages.description: [Aladdin commanding a genie to finish the window]
pages.scene: Aladdin commanding a genie to finish the window

pages.caption: Aladdin had won the hearts of the people by his gentle bearing. He was made captain of the Sultan's armies, and won several battles for him, but remained modest and courteous as before, and lived thus in peace and content for several years.
pages.description: [A prince leading armies to victory]
pages.scene: A prince leading armies to victory

pages.caption: But far away in Africa the magician remembered Aladdin, and by his magic arts discovered that Aladdin, instead of perishing miserably in the cave, had escaped, and had married a princess, with whom he was living in great honor and wealth.
pages.description: [A magician in a faraway land reading magic books]
pages.scene: A magician in a faraway land reading magic books

pages.caption: He knew that the poor tailor's son could only have accomplished this by means of the lamp, and traveled night and day until he reached the capital of China, bent on Aladdin's ruin.
pages.description: [A magician traveling by night]
pages.scene: A magician traveling by night

pages.caption: As he passed through the town he heard people talking everywhere about a marvellous palace. He bought a dozen copper lamps, put them into a basket, and went to the palace, crying: "New lamps for old!"
pages.description: [A man with a basket of copper lamps in the marketplace]
pages.scene: A man with a basket of copper lamps in the marketplace

pages.caption: The Princess, sitting in the hall of four-and-twenty windows, sent a slave to find out what the noise was about, who came back laughing.
pages.description: [A princess sending a slave to investigate]
pages.scene: A princess sending a slave to investigate

pages.caption: "Madam," replied the slave, "who can help laughing to see an old fool offering to exchange fine new lamps for old ones?"
pages.description: [A slave laughing about an old man's offer]
pages.scene: A slave laughing about an old man's offer

pages.caption: Another slave, hearing this, said: "There is an old one on the cornice there which he can have." Now this was the magic lamp, which Aladdin had left there, as he could not take it out hunting with him.
pages.description: [A slave taking a lamp from a cornice]
pages.scene: A slave taking a lamp from a cornice

pages.caption: The Princess, not knowing its value, laughingly bade the slave take it and make the exchange. She went and said to the magician: "Give me a new lamp for this." He snatched it and bade the slave take her choice.
pages.description: [A magician snatching a lamp with glee]
pages.scene: A magician snatching a lamp with glee

pages.caption: He left off crying his lamps, and went out of the city gates to a lonely place, where he remained till nightfall, when he pulled out the lamp and rubbed it.
pages.description: [A magician alone at night rubbing a lamp]
pages.scene: A magician alone at night rubbing a lamp

pages.caption: The genie appeared, and at the magician's command carried him, together with the palace and the Princess in it, to a lonely place in Africa.
pages.description: [A palace vanishing into thin air]
pages.scene: A palace vanishing into thin air

pages.caption: Next morning the Sultan looked out of the window toward Aladdin's palace and rubbed his eyes, for it was gone.
pages.description: [A Sultan staring at an empty horizon]
pages.scene: A Sultan staring at an empty horizon

pages.caption: He sent thirty men on horseback to fetch Aladdin in chains. They met him riding home, bound him, and forced him to go with them on foot.
pages.description: [A prince bound by soldiers]
pages.scene: A prince bound by soldiers

pages.caption: The people, however, who loved him, followed, armed, to see that he came to no harm. He was carried before the Sultan, who ordered the executioner to cut off his head.
pages.description: [A crowd rising to save a prince]
pages.scene: A crowd rising to save a prince

pages.caption: The executioner made Aladdin kneel down, bandaged his eyes, and raised his scimitar to strike. At that instant the Vizier, who saw that the crowd had forced their way into the courtyard and were scaling the walls to rescue Aladdin, called to the executioner to stay his hand.
pages.description: [A Sultan sparing a prince's life]
pages.scene: A Sultan sparing a prince's life

pages.caption: Aladdin now begged to know what he had done. "False wretch!" said the Sultan, "come thither," and showed him from the window the place where his palace had stood. Aladdin was so amazed that he could not say a word.
pages.description: [A prince wandering alone in despair]
pages.scene: A prince wandering alone in despair

pages.caption: For three days he wandered about like a madman, asking everyone what had become of his palace, but they only laughed and pitied him. He came to the banks of a river, and knelt down to say his prayers before throwing himself in.
pages.description: [A prince kneeling by a river in prayer]
pages.scene: A prince kneeling by a river in prayer

pages.caption: In so doing he rubbed the magic ring he still wore. The genie he had seen in the cave appeared, and asked his will. "Save my life, genie," said Aladdin, "bring my palace back."
pages.description: [A prince rubbing a ring and summoning a genie]
pages.scene: A prince rubbing a ring and summoning a genie

pages.caption: "That is not in my power," said the genie; "I am only the Slave of the Ring; you must ask him of the lamp." "Even so," said Aladdin, "but thou canst take me to the palace, and set me down under my dear wife's window."
pages.description: [A genie transporting a prince to Africa]
pages.scene: A genie transporting a prince to Africa

pages.caption: He at once found himself in Africa, under the window of the Princess, and fell asleep out of sheer weariness.
pages.description: [A prince falling asleep under a window]
pages.scene: A prince falling asleep under a window

pages.caption: That morning the Princess rose earlier than she had done since she had been carried into Africa by the magician. She ran and opened the window, and at the noise she made Aladdin looked up.
pages.description: [A princess opening a window to her beloved]
pages.scene: A princess opening a window to her beloved

pages.caption: She called to him to come to her, and great was the joy of these lovers at seeing each other again.
pages.description: [A prince and princess reunited]
pages.scene: A prince and princess reunited

pages.caption: After he had kissed her Aladdin said: "I beg of you, Princess, in God's name, before we speak of anything else, for your own sake and mine, tell me what has become of an old lamp I left on the cornice in the hall of four-and-twenty windows, when I went a-hunting."
pages.description: [A prince and princess whispering at a window]
pages.scene: A prince and princess whispering at a window

pages.caption: "Alas!" she said, "I am the innocent cause of our sorrows," and told him of the exchange of the lamp. "Now I know," cried Aladdin, "that we have to thank the African magician for this!"
pages.description: [A princess confessing with tears]
pages.scene: A princess confessing with tears

pages.caption: Aladdin comforted her, and left her for a while. He changed clothes with the first person he met in the town, and having bought a certain powder, returned to the Princess, who let him in by a little side door.
pages.description: [A prince disguised in common clothes]
pages.scene: A prince disguised in common clothes

pages.caption: "Put on your most beautiful dress," he said to her, "and receive the magician with smiles, leading him to believe that you have forgotten me. Invite him to sup with you, and say you wish to taste the wine of his country."
pages.description: [A prince giving instructions to a princess]
pages.scene: A prince giving instructions to a princess

pages.caption: She listened carefully to Aladdin and when he left she arrayed herself gaily for the first time since she left China. She put on a girdle and head-dress of diamonds, and, seeing in a glass that she was more beautiful than ever, received the magician.
pages.description: [A princess dressed in diamonds smiling at a magician]
pages.scene: A princess dressed in diamonds smiling at a magician

pages.caption: "I have made up my mind that Aladdin is dead, and that all my tears will not bring him back to me, so I am resolved to mourn no more, and have therefore invited you to sup with me; but I am tired of the wines of China, and would fain taste those of Africa."
pages.description: [A princess offering a cup to a magician]
pages.scene: A princess offering a cup to a magician

pages.caption: The magician flew to his cellar, and the Princess put the powder Aladdin had given her in her cup. When he returned she asked him to drink her health in the wine of Africa, handing him her cup in exchange for his, as a sign she was reconciled to him.
pages.description: [A magician draining a poisoned cup]
pages.scene: A magician draining a poisoned cup

pages.caption: Before drinking the magician made her a speech in praise of her beauty, but the Princess cut him short, saying: "Let us drink first, and you shall say what you will afterward." She set her cup to her lips and kept it there, while the magician drained his to the dregs and fell back lifeless.
pages.description: [A magician falling back lifeless]
pages.scene: A magician falling back lifeless

pages.caption: The Princess then opened the door to Aladdin, and flung her arms round his neck; but Aladdin put her away, bidding her leave him, as he had more to do. He then went to the dead magician, took the lamp out of his vest, and bade the genie carry the palace and all in it back to China.
pages.description: [A prince reclaiming a magic lamp]
pages.scene: A prince reclaiming a magic lamp

pages.caption: This was done, and the Princess in her chamber only felt two little shocks, and little thought she was at home again.
pages.description: [A palace returning to its original place]
pages.scene: A palace returning to its original place

pages.caption: The Sultan, who was sitting in his closet, mourning for his lost daughter, happened to look up, and rubbed his eyes, for there stood the palace as before!
pages.description: [A Sultan weeping in his closet]
pages.scene: A Sultan weeping in his closet

pages.caption: He hastened thither, and Aladdin received him in the hall of the four-and-twenty windows, with the Princess at his side. Aladdin told him what had happened, and showed him the dead body of the magician, that he might believe.
pages.description: [A Sultan embraced by his son-in-law]
pages.scene: A Sultan embraced by his son-in-law

pages.caption: A ten days' feast was proclaimed, and it seemed as if Aladdin might now live the rest of his life in peace; but it was not to be.
pages.description: [A ten days feast proclaimed]
pages.scene: A ten days feast proclaimed

pages.caption: The African magician had a younger brother, who was, if possible, more wicked and more cunning than himself. He traveled to China to avenge his brother's death, and went to visit a pious woman called Fatima.
pages.description: [A wicked brother of the magician]
pages.scene: A wicked brother of the magician

pages.caption: He entered her cell and clapped a dagger to her breast, telling her to rise and do his bidding on pain of death. He changed clothes with her, colored his face like hers, put on her veil, and murdered her, that she might tell no tales.
pages.description: [A man murdering a holy woman]
pages.scene: A man murdering a holy woman

pages.caption: Then he went toward the palace of Aladdin, and all the people, thinking he was the holy woman, gathered round him, kissing his hands and begging his blessing.
pages.description: [A false holy woman approaching the palace]
pages.scene: A false holy woman approaching the palace

pages.caption: When he got to the palace there was such a noise going on round him that the Princess bade her slave look out of the window and ask what was the matter. The slave said it was the holy woman, curing people by her touch of their ailments, whereupon the Princess, who had long desired to see Fatima, sent for her.
pages.description: [A princess welcoming a false holy woman]
pages.scene: A princess welcoming a false holy woman

pages.caption: On coming to the Princess the magician offered up a prayer for her health and prosperity. When he had done the Princess made him sit by her, and begged him to stay with her always. The false Fatima, who wished for nothing better, consented, but kept his veil down for fear of discovery. The Princess showed him the hall, and asked him what he thought of it. "It is truly beautiful," said the false Fatima. "In my mind it wants but one thing." "And what is that?" said the Princess. "If only a roc's egg," replied he, "were hung up from the middle of this dome, it would be the wonder of the world."
pages.description: [A false holy woman suggesting a roc's egg]
pages.scene: A false holy woman suggesting a roc's egg

pages.caption: After this the Princess could think of nothing but the roc's egg, and when Aladdin returned from hunting he found her in a very ill humor. He begged to know what was amiss, and she told him that all her pleasure in the hall was spoiled for the want of a roc's egg hanging from the dome.
pages.description: [A princess pouting and displeased]
pages.scene: A princess pouting and displeased

pages.caption: "If that is all," replied Aladdin, "you shall soon be happy." He left her and rubbed the lamp, and when the genie appeared commanded him to bring a roc's egg.
pages.description: [A prince commanding a genie]
pages.scene: A prince commanding a genie

pages.caption: The genie gave such a loud and terrible shriek that the hall shook. "Wretch!" he cried, "is it not enough that I have done everything for you, but you must command me to bring my master and hang him up in the midst of this dome?"
pages.description: [A genie shrieking in fury]
pages.scene: A genie shrieking in fury

pages.caption: "You and your wife and your palace deserve to be burnt to ashes, but that this request does not come from you, but from the brother of the African magician, whom you destroyed. He is now in your palace disguised as the holy woman--whom he murdered."
pages.description: [A genie revealing the truth to a prince]
pages.scene: A genie revealing the truth to a prince

pages.caption: Aladdin went back to the Princess, saying his head ached, and requesting that the holy Fatima should be fetched to lay her hands on it. But when the magician came near, Aladdin, seizing his dagger, pierced him to the heart.
pages.description: [A prince seizing a dagger]
pages.scene: A prince seizing a dagger

pages.caption: "What have you done?" cried the Princess. "You have killed the holy woman!" "Not so," replied Aladdin, "but a wicked magician," and told her of how she had been deceived.
pages.description: [A prince and princess together in peace]
pages.scene: A prince and princess together in peace

pages.caption: After this Aladdin and his wife lived in peace. He succeeded the Sultan when he died, and reigned for many years, leaving behind him a long line of kings.
pages.description: [A king on a throne with his queen]
pages.scene: A king on a throne with his queen
